name: Dmitry Medvedev
role: Russian politician: President 2008-2012, Prime Minister 2012-2020, Deputy Chairman of the Security Council since 2020
summary: Medvedev's presidential-era texts (the 2008 address, 'Go Russia!') argue for gradual modernisation, a market economy freed of bureaucracy, democracy introduced step by step and a well-armed Russia; as president he recognised South Ossetia and Abkhazia and justified the 2008 Georgia operation as protecting civilians.

democracy-best.rationale: In 2008 he told the Federal Assembly 'democracy is the way forward, and no one disputes this now' and called democratic freedoms 'the source for our continued development'; in 2009 he wrote 'Democracy needs to be protected', while rejecting a copy of foreign models and any rush to speed up reform. Neither text addresses voters choosing badly.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In 'Go Russia!' he named the CSTO, EurAsEC and CIS countries 'our closest, strategic partners' with whom 'we must increase our cooperation', and in 2008 said Russia would 'increase the volume and scope of our cooperation in the military and political spheres in the CSTO'.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Among his five strategic vectors in 'Go Russia!' he wrote that 'we need to maintain and raise our nuclear technology to a qualitatively new level'; the text does not speak of power plants specifically.

force-without-un.rationale: The August 2008 operation he ordered in Georgia was argued by Russia on grounds of defending its peacekeepers, protecting its citizens under Article 61(2) of its Constitution and protecting South Ossetian civilians; the EU fact-finding mission, which examined each of those grounds, names no Security Council mandate for it.

gradual-change.rationale: In 'Go Russia!' he told supporters of 'permanent revolution': 'We will not rush. Hasty and ill-considered political reforms have led to tragic consequences more than once in our history'; in 2008 he called for 'adjustments' to the Constitution, saying 'There is no place for a reforming itch' and that its basic provisions 'should remain unchanged for many years to come'.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In a January 2024 Telegram post he cited point 19 of Russia's nuclear deterrence policy, under which conventional aggression threatening the state's existence is 'a direct and obvious basis for the use of nuclear weapons', warning those who attack Russia.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: On 8 April 2010 he signed New START in Prague, which cuts each side to 700 deployed launchers, 1550 deployed warheads and 800 launchers in all but keeps those arsenals, lets each party decide its own force structure and allows withdrawal if its 'supreme interests' are jeopardized.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 'Go Russia!' he attributed corruption to 'the excessive government presence' in economic life, and in 2008 he called the state bureaucracy, as 'biggest employer... best producer', 'a completely ineffective system' that 'leads only to corruption'; he also asked the state to set the strategic priorities (see state-directs-investment).

military-superiority.rationale: In November 2008 he reversed the planned disbanding of the Kozelsk missile division, ordering that 'nothing will disband', and ordered Iskander missiles deployed in Kaliningrad and jamming of the planned US missile-defence installations from there; he also said Russia would not be 'dragged into an arms race'.

multipolar-world.rationale: In his 2009 CNN interview he said 'we are living in a multi-polar world which is acknowledged by everybody today' and that Russia counts on good relations 'not only with the western world but also with the other parts of the planet'; he describes the world rather than urging it.

national-self-determination.rationale: On 26 August 2008 he signed decrees recognising the independence of South Ossetia and of Abkhazia, two regions that had broken away from Georgia. The act recognises two peoples' claim to statehood; it is not a general rule for every people.

party-controls-media.rationale: In 2008 he listed among the bureaucracy's faults that it 'takes control of this or that media outlet, trying to stop it from saying what they consider the wrong thing', and in 2009 told CNN 'trying to curtail press freedom is a totally hopeless thing to do', while admitting pressure on journalists, mostly by regional bosses, and that Russia is not 'an ideal world'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In 'Go Russia!' he wrote that Russia must protect 'our historical heritage from distortion and political speculations' and that, of its traditions, 'only unquestionable values which must be preserved' count, naming interethnic and interfaith peace, military valour, duty and hospitality, and calling bribery, theft and drunkenness vices that 'offend our traditions'.

property-fundamental.rationale: In his 2008 address he called the 1993 Constitution, 'proclaiming the individual, their life, rights and property as the highest value', 'an unprecedented event in Russia's history' for which 'we should thank all those who took part'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In 'Go Russia!' he named 'five strategic vectors for the economic modernisation of our country' (energy efficiency, nuclear technology, information technology, space and satellite infrastructure, medicine) as the state's priorities for developing the economy away from raw materials.

notes: A new audit built from his own Kremlin-published texts of the presidency (the 2008 Address to the Federal Assembly, the 'Go Russia!' article, the 26 August 2008 statement) and a CNN transcript of 8 August 2008. Eighteen statements answered. The interviews in the local news corpus (CNN, NPR, 2008-2010) were read for the Georgia war, Iran, sanctions and press freedom; they repeat or add nothing a statement turns on beyond the cited texts. Deeper pass: New START (signing record and treaty text), Libya 2011 (UN Security Council record of Russia's abstention; his own statement of 21 March 2011 is read but not cited because the answers rest on the act), and his Telegram channel read by theme (about 250 posts, Nov 2023 to Nov 2026): one post on nuclear deterrence is cited. His posts calling Ukraine 'not a country' (12 Nov 2023) sit against his 2008 recognition of two breakaway regions, so national-self-determination keeps the act-based answer; his posts on strikes on Kyiv and European arms plants state no position that settles a statement without an inference. The 2008 amendment lengthening presidential terms was not available as a text to cite (address cited only for his proposal), so term-limits and unlimited-reelection stay null. The uncertainty rule is not met.
